standard_prerequisites.name: Standard convex polytope theory: faces, face lattices, normal cones and normal fans
standard_prerequisites.reference: G. M. Ziegler, Lectures on Polytopes, and the article's own conventions at source line 511
standard_prerequisites.use: Only the standard notion of normally equivalent polytopes (same normal fan) and elementary face/cone duality are assumed. The normal-cone characterisation of the diagonal image and the induced canonical equivalence of the two subdivisions remain the retained obligations.

standard_prerequisites.name: Polar cones and the polar cone theorem for closed convex cones
standard_prerequisites.reference: standard finite-dimensional convexity (Rockafellar); used at source lines 1136-1143
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof quotes the polar cone theorem to identify the polar of P-y with the normal cone of the face through y. That theorem is not re-proved; every step that involves the orientation vector, the diagonal map and the two subdivisions is the retained author argument.

core_obligations: Restate membership (x,y) in im(triangle_P), for x in the relative interior of a face F and y in the relative interior of a face G, as the non-existence of a vector w with <v,w> > 0 and w in -N_P(F)^* cap N_P(G)^* (source lines 1134-1146).

Identify the polar of P-y with the normal cone of the face whose relative interior contains y via the polar cone theorem, so that the membership test depends only on the normal fan of P (lines 1142-1146).

Conclude that when P and Q are normally equivalent and well-oriented by the same vector v, the map Phi x Phi on face lattices induces the canonical combinatorial equivalence of the tight coherent subdivisions F_(P,v) and F_(Q,v) (lines 1147-1148).
proof_roadmap: Normal equivalence of P and Q gives a face-lattice isomorphism Phi: L(P) -> L(Q).
Characterise im(triangle_P): (x,y) is in it exactly when no w with <v,w> > 0 admits x - eps w in P and y + eps w in P for some eps > 0.

Translate that into polar cones: (P-y)^* is the normal cone N_P(G) of the face G whose relative interior contains y, so the condition is that the cone -N_P(F)^* cap N_P(G)^* contains no vector with positive pairing against v.
Since the condition only refers to normal cones and the orientation vector, Phi x Phi carries the subdivision of P to the subdivision of Q canonically.
difficulty_reason: The proposition compares two polytopes that are only normally equivalent, and its proof must first replace the definition of the diagonal by a normal-fan condition: for x in the relative interior of a face F and y in the relative interior of a face G, the pair (x,y) lies in im(triangle_P) exactly when no vector w with <v,w> > 0 lies in -N_P(F)^* cap N_P(G)^* (source lines 1134-1146). This rests on the polar-cone description of the normal cone of the face through y and on the orientation hypotheses on (P,v) and (Q,v), not on the face lattices alone. The step that cannot be done routinely is turning that membership test into a canonical combinatorial equivalence of the two tight coherent subdivisions, because the equivalence has to be induced by Phi x Phi on the face lattices (lines 1147-1148) rather than asserted from normal equivalence; standard normal-fan theory contains no diagonal-specific statement of this kind.
